title_en: Alashankou Company v. Ningxia Qinyi Company — jurisdictional objection in a sales contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of Article 25 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinion on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, in cases where the parties have agreed by contract that they may file lawsuits at the people's court of either party's domicile, if either party files a lawsuit and the court at its domicile accepts the case, the other party's request to the court at its own domicile for duplicate filing or to transfer the case to its domicile court shall be dismissed.

full_text_en:
Alashankou Xinke Co., Ltd. v. Ningxia Qinyi Industrial Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over sales contract (objection to jurisdiction)

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 25 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, where the parties have agreed by contract that either party may bring a lawsuit in the people's court of its own domicile, and one party has filed a lawsuit which has been accepted by the court of its domicile, the other party's request that the court of its own domicile docket a duplicate action or transfer the case to its domicile court shall be dismissed.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 94

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Ningxia Qinyi Industrial Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: North Street, Zhongning County, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Qin Jun, General Manager of the Company.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Alashankou Xinke Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jungar Road, Alashankou, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Song Daocheng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The appellant, Ningxia Qinyi Industrial Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ningxia Qinyi Company), appealed against the civil ruling of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (2005) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 8-2 in a dispute over a sales contract with the appellee, Alashankou Xinke Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Alashankou Company), to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Zhou Fan serving as presiding judge, and Acting Judges Jia Wei and Sha Ling as members, to hear the case. Yuan Hongxia served as the court clerk. The case is now concluded.

Found facts: The two agreements on the basis of which Alashankou Company filed the lawsuit in this case each provided: "If disputes arise during the execution of the contract, the parties shall resolve them through friendly negotiation; if negotiation fails, the parties may bring a lawsuit in the people's court of their respective domiciles." During the first instance, Ningxia Qinyi Company raised an objection to jurisdiction, arguing that the aforesaid agreement on jurisdiction by contract violated Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and should be deemed invalid; it requested that the case be transferred to the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, being the place of contract performance and the defendant's domicile. Upon review, the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region held that, according to the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Determine Jurisdiction Where Both Parties to a Contract Have Agreed That Either Party May Bring a Lawsuit in the People's Court of Its Own Locale, the jurisdictional agreement in the contract was valid and should be used to determine the jurisdiction over this case. The court therefore, in accordance with Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled to dismiss Ningxia Qinyi Company's objection to jurisdiction.

Ningxia Qinyi Company, dissatisfied with the above civil ruling of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, appealed to this Court, arguing: The first instance court's reliance on the Supreme People's Court's reply as the basis for determining jurisdiction over this case constituted improper application of law; according to Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the provision in the contract that "the parties may bring a lawsuit in the people's court of their respective domiciles" should be deemed invalid. It requested that the case be transferred to the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region for jurisdiction.

Upon review, this Court holds: Pursuant to the provision in the contract that "if disputes arise during the execution of the contract, the parties may bring a lawsuit in the people's court of their respective domiciles," although both parties have the right to file a lawsuit and the people's courts of their respective domiciles each have jurisdiction, according to Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, where one party has filed a lawsuit and it has been accepted by the court of its domicile, the people's court of the other party's domicile may not docket a duplicate action, thereby excluding the jurisdiction of the other party's domicile court. Therefore, the substance of this agreement is to select the people's court of the plaintiff's domicile as the forum. This agreement does not constitute "choosing two or more people's courts from among those specified in Article 25 of the Civil Procedure Law," and is fully consistent with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on jurisdiction by agreement. It should be deemed valid and used to determine jurisdiction over this case. The first instance court's ruling to dismiss Ningxia Qinyi Company's objection to jurisdiction is well-founded and correctly applied the law, and should be affirmed; the grounds of appeal by Ningxia Qinyi Company are all untenable, and its request to transfer this case to the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region for jurisdiction should be dismissed. In accordance with Articles 25 and 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original ruling is affirmed.

Appeal case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by Ningxia Qinyi Industrial Group Co., Ltd.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhou Fan
Acting Judge: Jia Wei
Acting Judge: Sha Ling

June 6, 2005

Court Clerk: Yuan Hongxia

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Zhou Fan, Senior Judge: born in 1962, Bachelor of Laws, served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Second Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court since 2005.
